subject: No check on the data argument given to inla

messages.author: 93f93e99d1eec3f2
messages.subject: No check on the data argument given to inla
parts:
Dear Help,

I have stumbled across an interesting feature of INLA.

The inla function needs a data argument but actually if it does not contain the right variables then inla will look for it in the global environment as glm.nb from MASS does for example.

I must say I thought it was quite good for inla to force one to give a data argument. Maybe it could give a warning when the variables for fitting the model are not found in the data given to inla?

Here an example to explain what I mean.

nbVariable <- rnbinom(n1, mu = 10, size = 0.5)
formula <- as.formula(nbVariable ~ 1)
E <- mean(nbVariable)
dataModel <- as.data.frame(rnorm(1))
# INLA fitting
results <- inla(formula,data=dataModel,
                family='nbinomial',E=E)

It works and uses nbVariable from the global environment since dataModel does not provide the right variable.

Of course this
nbVariable <- rnbinom(n1, mu = 10, size = 0.5)
formula <- as.formula(miscellaneous ~ 1)
E <- mean(nbVariable)
dataModel <- as.data.frame(rnorm(1))
# INLA fitting
results <- inla(formula,data=dataModel,
                family='nbinomial',E=E)
does not work since there is no variable called "miscellaneous".

Best wishes

Maëlle.

On Mon, 2014-11-03 at 18:23 -0800, Daniel Simpson wrote:
Hi

having thought of this, I recall we have discussed it internally earlier
as well, and its all about 'design'.

if we have

y = -1
n = -1
r = inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y=1, n=1),
family = "binomial", Ntrials = n)

then inla will use y=1 and n=1 for 'y' and 'n', as it will look in
'data' first.

the issue is what will happen if we refer to a variable not in 'data',
like

YY = -1
r = inla(YY ~ 1, data = data.frame(y=1, n=1),
family = "binomial", Ntrials = n)

then it will use 'YY=-1' as 'YY' is not in data. Should we give an error
or warning in this case?? packages like 'glm' and 'lm' have this
behaviour (and this behaviour is kind of built into R) hence we do not
break any R 'style' or 'feature'.

would be nice to have a 'strict' mode, like setting an option would
make the above fail or give a warning. I agree. This would detect an
error if all variables was intentially defined by 'data'. I have looked
over the code, and its messy, and to be honest, I do not have full
control over what is going on or how this works.

one way might be to use

inla.strict = function(...)
{
<<<do something here>>>
return(inla(...))
}


where the missing code prevents one from assessing variables in unwanted
environments. I cannot see how this is done though...


H
